mara: heads-up — staging dedicated p99 jumped ~2.1x after onboarding model-2.1.0 (checkpoint + tokenizer remap). Canaries show KV-cache churn and kernel selection flip. pausing canary. :warning:
perf-monitor: CI perf test FAILED for model-2.1.0: p50 95ms -> 120ms, p99 190ms -> 410ms. failing test: infra/bench/p99_smoke. (run 2024-06-04T15:20Z)
sumit: ack. do we have the offending commit? any profiler traces?
mara: onboarding PR was abc1234 — tokenizer id-remap + small checkpoint metadata tweak. Also there was a change in kernel-selector heuristics in def4567 that landed three commits before. full stack trace attached in the PR but quick logs:
```
2024-06-04T15:18:02Z kernel-selector: selected kernel=matmul_large_batch for batch_size=2 seq_len=64
2024-06-04T15:18:02Z kv-cache: evict_rate spike=3.2x keys/sec
2024-06-04T15:18:02Z inference: p99=412ms, backend=coralv2, kernel_path=large_batch_path
```
sumit: interesting — kernel-selector chose large-batch kernel for tiny batches (batch_size=2). that explains extra kernel-launch overhead and KV thrash. will run a focused bisect between def4567 and abc1234.
alex: i ran a quick bisect — kernel-selector heuristic change (def4567) flips tiebreaker to favor throughput kernel when sequence_len >= 32 even for batch_size < 4. For our new tokenizer remap, average seq_len histogram shifted right (more 40-60 tokens) so the selector picks the wrong kernel.
ivy: also seeing KV key prefix change from tokenizer remap. remapped EOS -> new id causes prefix collisions in our kv key fn; leads to more misses and cache churn for short prefixes. combined effect is p99 surge.
perf-monitor: profiling snapshot: top spans:
- kernel_launch_overhead: +120ms
- kv_evictions: +90ms
- scheduler_spin: +40ms
(repro run: staging/dedicated/coralv2/replica-3)
sumit: options: 1) revert def4567 (kernel-selector change) 2) patch selector to prefer low-latency kernel when batch_size < 4 3) roll back tokenizer remap in model-2.1.0. prefer minimal blast radius.
mara: canary paused. recommending patch (2) first since it targets root cause faster than full revert. open to revert if patch risky. @deploy-bot please block rollout until we have an approved patch or revert. :no_entry:
deploy-bot: Canary paused by mara. rollout blocked for model-2.1.0.
sumit: i'll prototype selector patch now. quick local repro command:
```
./run_bench --model model-2.1.0 --bench seq_hist=short:80,mid:200 --batch-sizes=1,2,4 --trace kernel,kv
```
alex: i can validate kv prefix fix for tokenizer but that touches token ids in the checkpoint packaging — higher risk. i prefer selector patch + KV prefix mitigations (collision-resistant hashing) as a follow-up.
ivy: opened a tiny repro trace dump at https://s3.redwood/prof-traces/1717777777/model-2.1.0-trace.json :eyes:
sumit: drafted PR with selector patch (PR #3147) — changes tiebreaker to prefer low-latency kernel when batch_size < 4 or estimated_prefix_hits > 0. running CI perf locally now.
ci-bot: PR 3147 — perf checks: p99 delta ~= +5% (within noise) on baseline; staging rerun queued.
mara: awesome. once CI passes, we can unpause canary for a narrow shard and monitor kv evictions for 30m. if anything looks bad -> revert.
alex: created follow-up issue to re-evaluate tokenizer remap (ISSUE-1893) and to add unit test for kv key collisions.
mara: assign sumit, alex. thanks. :thumbsup:
sumit: noted, will post final status when CI green and canary resumed.
mara: status update 15:30Z — PR 3147 CI passed, canary resumed on 10% traffic. monitoring dashboards wired.
perf-monitor: canary graphs show p99 trending back to baseline after selector patch. kv-eviction rate down to normal.
mara: closing this thread after 1h watch unless we see regression. filing postmortem checklist items.
